original_finding.title: Relevant MG uptake modulation and its internal source tension lack a disposition

evidence.interpretation: In induced MC4100 uptake experiments, Results reports weak effects of glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller trehalose effect, and no effect for fructose and the named non-PTS comparators. Discussion describes mannose and the three glycosyl analogues as not significantly inhibitory even at 1 mM against 0.1 μM radiolabeled MG. These statements must coexist, rather than being upgraded into a robust direct competitive-inhibition mechanism. The same Results also reports that 300 mM NaCl did not induce transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by approximately half; this differs from the later KM522 500 mM salt-protection test.

original_finding.rationale: The linked entry event is explicitly in record scope, yet these source-supported experimental bounds are absent from target, authored research and scope disposition. This is material incompleteness of the entry mechanism context, not a demand to extend unrelated regulons.
original_finding.fix: Preserve the observed weak-positive and negative uptake comparisons, the Results/Discussion mannose tension, and the separate salt-induction observation in source-backed entry assay context and corresponding scope/coverage ledgers. Keep MC4100 and measured uptake/induction endpoints explicit. Do not assert direct ligand binding, a competitive mechanism, exact inhibition constants or a stronger biological sign than the source supports. If graph edges are added, independently ground each chemical and qualify the measured process; source-limited prose on the existing entry context is acceptable where exact mechanistic/chemical scope is unresolved.
acceptance: Relevant source statements are present with exact L-number locators and declared projection access.
The mannose weak-effect/no-significant-effect tension and negative controls remain explicit.
300 mM salt-induced suppression of induction is separated from KM522 osmoprotection and from a direct catalytic salt effect.
Original two core events and native 17 chemical sides remain unchanged.
original_finding.author_response: Author independently acknowledged no explicit evidence-backed exclusion was preserved; this does not replace reviewer inspection.

original_finding.title: CdaR assay-derived regulatory endpoints omit construct and sequence-reference qualification

evidence.interpretation: The study uses MC4100 loss/rescue and reporter systems; its reference describes 391 residues, paper-numbered P297S in JA176 and a near-terminal Tn5 insertion in JA177. pRM1 carries MC4100 sdaR in pBluescript. Positive autoregulation is inferred from reporter responses and loss of functional sdaR.
The current issuing reference is P37047 with 385 residues. The author dossier retains this mismatch, but it is not on either regulatory subject endpoint in the YAML/page/export claim.

original_finding.rationale: The graph/export endpoint is the exact modern reference protein. Assay-specific reference numbering, preparations and loss/rescue interpretation must travel with the affected claim, rather than remaining only in an external dossier. The signs and gene endpoints are supported; this is a scope defect, not evidence that P297S or Tn5 mutants activate transcription.
original_finding.fix: Qualify the subject of both affected edges as experimental_construct with exact source-limited MC4100 reporter/loss/rescue context and the 391-aa paper/current-385-aa reference distinction. Preserve paper residue numbering without silently mapping it to the modern chain. Distinguish active reference or rescued regulator from loss-of-function mutants used to infer its role; do not mint a new protein ID or label mutant proteins as active.
acceptance: Both affected CdaR subject endpoints retain evidence-backed qualification in YAML, graph and KGX.
Current P37047 identity and both existing positive expression signs/gene targets remain unchanged.
No asserted sequence equivalence, direct ligand binding or active P297S/Tn5 phenotype is introduced.
original_finding.author_response: Author acknowledged intended native activation supported by loss/rescue, and confirmed the missing target-level preparation/reference distinction.
